title: I Let the Office Hot-Sauce Fridge Ban Catch the Person Who Wrote It

parts.text: I opened the break-room fridge at 12:03 p.m. and a new memo banned unlabeled condiments because of a spill. The memo author, Greg, had three unlabeled mini-bottles of a sauce so hot it had a skull. I was twenty-six, support tech, holding a turkey sandwich. I labeled my mustard. I also labeled Greg's skull bottles with his name from the memo footer. He said that was aggressive. At 12:11 facilities asked who owned the leak that was still dripping from a skull cap onto the crisper.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Facilities can see the drip and the name I wrote from his own footer.

social.video_title: He banned unlabeled bottles and left a skull dripping — Part 1/2
social.description: Mustard labeled, memo footer, crisper leak. Aggressive was a Sharpie. Would you have named the skulls?

parts.text: Greg claimed the bottles. The ban stayed. Unlabeled meant unlabeled. I ate turkey with mustard that had a name. The crisper got a wipe. Skull caps now live in Greg's desk, which is a fridge if you are committed. The memo did not get a Greg exception. Footers are signatures. I keep a Sharpie in the utensil cup. Spills have authors.
